answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The signal multiplier is published, charged in wander, and tundra lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3363 identities would post 4202 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
